subject: Request: IR plan + SIG/CAIQ/SOC2 artifacts and postmortem for Feb 12 event
messages:
From: Amanda Chen <amanda.chen@medsys.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: secops@medsys.com
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request for IRP and compliance artifacts after Feb 12 disruption

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick updates on Feb 12 — our integration with your embeddings endpoint had a brief disruption that impacted batch indexing overnight. As part of our internal audit and SOC 2 evidence collection, we need the following from Redwood: 

- The current Incident Response Plan (IRP) you maintain for production incidents (PDF or link).
- SIG/CAIQ questionnaire responses or a filled template for our security team.
- SOC 2 cover letter indicating scope and latest audit date.
- A short postmortem / timeline for the Feb 12 event and the mitigations applied.
- Sample logs (redacted) showing request IDs and error traces for our affected window (we will treat these as sensitive).

We understand some items may be redacted — please indicate what was redacted and why. Ideally we’d like these artifacts by EOD Monday (Feb 15) so Compliance can close the ticket. If you prefer a quick call to walk through the artifacts, please propose a time.

Appreciate it —
Amanda Chen
Senior IT Security Manager
MediSys Health
amanda.chen@medsys.com

---
Attachment: screenshot_20270212_error.png (image/png - referenced)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Chen <amanda.chen@medsys.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request for IRP and compliance artifacts after Feb 12 disruption

Amanda — thanks for the note and the screenshot. Apologies again for the disruption; I wanted to acknowledge receipt and outline what we can provide by your EOD Mon target.

What we will deliver by Monday 17:00 PT:
- Redwood_IRP_v1.2.pdf (production IRP, high-level playbooks and escalation matrix).
- SIG/CAIQ response spreadsheet (SIG_CAIX_responses.xlsx) with callouts for restricted answers.
- SOC2_cover_letter.pdf summarizing scope and most recent audit quarter.
- A concise postmortem (MSH_postmortem_20270212.docx) with a 1-page timeline and root cause.
- Sample logs exported and redacted (logs_sample_redacted.ndjson) covering the 02/12 01:30-03:15 UTC window you flagged — fields PII-redacted per our policy.

Notes on redaction and scope: we will remove full user PII (email, phone) from logs and replace with hashed IDs; request IDs and timestamps will be preserved. The SIG file will flag any questions we cannot fully disclose (vendor internal configs) and provide compensating controls. If you need raw unredacted logs under an NDA, please indicate and we can route via your legal/compliance contact.

If you prefer a walkthrough, I can join a 30-minute call; Marissa will coordinate scheduling. Proposed slots: Mon 10:00 PT, Mon 13:30 PT, Mon 16:00 PT.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Security Operations | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0182

Attachment: none (documents to follow)

From: Amanda Chen <amanda.chen@medsys.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, secops@medsys.com
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 07:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request for IRP and compliance artifacts after Feb 12 disruption

Karthik — thanks, that timeline and scope helps. A couple of quick follow-ups before your deliverable: 

1) Retention: can you confirm your default request/trace log retention for production telemetry (hot + cold tiers) and whether any accelerated purge was done for the Feb 12 event?
2) PII: you mentioned hashed IDs — what hashing algorithm and salt approach do you use? Our Compliance team needs to verify that data is irreversible for our scope.
3) SLA credits / impact: our Procurement team will want the postmortem to call out whether the event qualified for SLA remediation and your proposed remediation (if any).

We can take the SLA/credits discussion offline with Marissa. If possible, please include a short paragraph in the postmortem that explicitly states whether this incident meets your SLA "major outage" threshold.

I’ll plan to review the artifacts once shared. Please also include a link to the IRP in your corporate drive (if that’s easier than attaching the full PDF).

-Amanda

---
Attachment: n/a

From: monica_patel@redwood.com <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Chen <amanda.chen@medsys.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 11:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request for IRP and compliance artifacts after Feb 12 disruption

Amanda — looping in Marissa to handle the SLA/contract side; I’ve attached the initial artifacts and a short postmortem summary as promised. Quick answers inline: 

- Retention: production request traces are retained in hot tier for 30 days, then archived for 365 days in compressed cold storage. No expedited purge was performed for this event.
- Hashing: we use SHA-256 with a per-tenant salt rotated quarterly; salted hashes are irreversible for practical purposes and we do not store the raw salt alongside logs. We can share our hashing policy doc under NDA.
- SLA: the Feb 12 disruption did not meet our internal "major outage" criteria (total customer-impacting error rate < 0.05% over a 60m window). We documented mitigations and a configuration fix (edge retry tuning); no SLA credits are being offered for this incident.

Attachments included: Redwood_IRP_v1.2.pdf; MSH_postmortem_20270212.docx; SOC2_cover_letter.pdf; SIG_CAIX_responses.xlsx; logs_sample_redacted.ndjson.

If you’d like a 20–30 minute walkthrough, here’s a booking link: https://calendly.com/redwood-security/30min. Marissa will coordinate procurement follow-up on SLA language.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Director, Customer Security & Trust | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
